List, delete or undelete sets, or show and change a set's retention

```sh
goback [global flags] set <command>
```

## set list

List the sets with what their agents expect of them and whether they are late

```sh
goback [global flags] set list
```

## set delete

Close a set and retire its commits; --erase skips the trash window

```sh
goback [global flags] set delete [flags] <name>
```

| Flag | Description | Environment | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--erase` | tombstone the commits now instead of after the trash window |  |  |

## set undelete

Reopen a set before its commits are tombstoned

```sh
goback [global flags] set undelete <name>
```

## set retention

Show or change a set's retention policy, or the store's default when no name is given; a keep flag replaces the policy, --inherit removes it

```sh
goback [global flags] set retention [flags] [<name>]
```

| Flag | Description | Environment | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--keep-last value` | keep this many of the newest commits |  |  |
| `--keep value` | keep the last commit of each of the latest &lt;count&gt; calendar periods, given as &lt;period&gt;=&lt;count&gt;; repeat it for each bracket, newest first; the last bracket may omit its count to keep forever (--keep hourly=336 --keep daily=60 --keep weekly=12 --keep monthly) |  |  |
| `--keep-within value` | keep every commit younger than this |  |  |
| `--inherit` | remove the policy, so a set follows the store's policy and the store follows the built-in one |  |  |
| `--trash-days value` | store only: how many days a deleted commit waits before it is tombstoned |  | `-1` |
